articles.title: Philippines, Poland ink mutual legal assistance pact
articles.summary: The Philippines and Poland yesterday signed an agreement on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, as leaders of both countries expect expanded relations in economy, information technology,…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am

President Marcos shakes hands with Poland President Karol Nawrocki at Malacañang on October 6, 2026. This marks the first-ever state visit by a Polish head of state to the Philippines since diplomatic relations were established in 1973.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Poland yesterday signed an agreement on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters, as leaders of both countries expect expanded relations in economy, information technology, defense as well as a strategic partnership amid security threats facing the two nations.
President Marcos welcomed Polish President Karol Nawrocki and his delegation at Malacañang, where the latter was accorded arrival honors.
This is the first visit of a head of state of the Republic of Poland to the Philippines.

At a joint press conference at Malacañang, Marcos highlighted the two countries’ ongoing and future cooperation in key areas such as defense and security, trade, industry, agriculture, science and technology, information and communications technology, energy, legal cooperation and people-to-people relations.
The President also cited the Philippines’ acquisition of S-70 Black Hawk combat utility helicopters from Poland as part of the modernization program of the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

He said the two countries look forward to building on the outcomes of the inaugural Philippines-Poland Joint Defense Cooperation Committee, including through joint training and educational opportunities.
Poland has been participating as an observer in the Balikatan Exercises since 2025.

“President Nawrocki and I also had insightful exchange of views on regional and international matters of mutual concern, including the challenges in the South China Sea and security developments in Ukraine and in Europe,” Marcos said.
“We reiterated our shared commitment to upholding the rule of law in international relations and the peaceful resolution of conflicts,” Marcos said.

For his part, Nawrocki said defense cooperation is an important aspect of the two countries’ relations, as security challenges face by Europe and the Indo-Pacific “can no longer be approached separately.”
“We want to develop this cooperation also in other areas,” the Polish leader said, noting that the IT sector is one of the important areas of potential cooperation between Warsaw and Manila.
“We have discussed maritime security, state resilience, cyber security, also about the security of strategic supply chains,” Nawrocki said.
“Today we want, and we are opening a new chapter in these relations. Poland is very much interested in raising our relationship to the level of a strategic partnership,” he noted.
Marcos said he and Nawrocki reaffirmed the two countries’ respect for international law.
“And of course, these incursions or attempts to change territorial definitions are unacceptable in both Poland and in the Philippines,” he said.
Nawrocki will inaugurate today the fifth edition of the Polish-Filipino Economic IT Summit in Manila.
He also asked the Philippines’ support for Poland’s permanent membership in the G20, as it is the 20th largest economy in the world, and has invited Marcos to visit Warsaw.
The two countries signed the Agreement on a Transfer of Sentenced Persons earlier this year.
Manila and Warsaw also affirmed their readiness to commence negotiations on an extradition agreement, Marcos said.

articles.title: Government urges SC: Junk petition vs BSKE postponement
articles.summary: The Supreme Court should dismiss the challenge to the law fixing the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections officials and resetting the election to November 2028, as well as deny efforts…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am

High school students sign up for the barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections at the Commission on Elections satellite voter’s registration site at the Pinaglabanan Elementary School in San Juan, in this file photo from August 2025.
Miguel De Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court should dismiss the challenge to the law fixing the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) officials and resetting the election to November 2028, as well as deny efforts to prevent its enforcement, several government agencies appealed.

The Office of the Solicitor General (OSG), which represented the Office of the President, the Senate, the House of Representatives and the Commission on Elections (Comelec), filed on Oct. 5 its 64-page comment to the petition for certiorari and prohibition submitted by election lawyer Romulo Macalintal.

The comment disputed Macalintal’s arguments in his petition filed on Sept. 27, including his claim that Republic Act 12326, which fixed the term of barangay and SK officials from four to five years and rescheduled their election to November 2028, “infringes the electorate’s right of suffrage by postponing the November 2026 BSKE under the guise of fixing terms.”

RA 12326, signed into law by President Marcos on Sept. 24, moved the next regular BSKE from Nov. 2, 2026 to the second Monday of November 2028 and set succeeding elections every five years. It also fixed the term of barangay and SK officials at five years.
“RA 12326 is a valid term-fixing law. Hence, the 2023 Macalintal guidelines do not apply to the present case,” the OSG declared.

The agency referred to RA 12232, which set the term of barangay and SK officials to four years and scheduled the election to the first Monday of November 2026, in justifying the validity of RA 12326 that scheduled the next BSKE to the second Monday of November 2028.

“Like RA 12232, the main purpose of RA 12326 is to extend the terms of BSK officials from four years to five years. The resulting postponement of elections is but a logistical consequence of the term extension,” according to the OSG.
It also maintained that Congress has the discretion to set the terms of barangay and SK officials.

“It is a political question which brings to the fore the wisdom of the law, taking into account both Congress’ role as legislators and as representatives of the people keenly aware of the realities at the grassroots level,” said the OSG.
TRO urgently sought
Macalintal, however, renewed his plea for the SC to stop the implementation of RA 12326.
In an urgent omnibus motion and reply filed electronically with the SC yesterday, Macalintal reiterated his request for a temporary restraining order and/or status quo ante order.

He also asked the court to direct the Comelec to resume preparations for the Nov. 2 BSKE or, if the polls could no longer be held on that date, conduct them on a date reasonably close to it under the Omnibus Election Code.

Macalintal disputed the government’s interpretation, pointing to Section 5 of RA 12326, which states” “Considering the extension of their terms by two (2) years, incumbent elective barangay officials shall be regarded as having completed one (1) term in their respective positions.”
“If this is not an extension of the term of incumbent barangay officials, then what is?” Macalintal said.
He argued that Congress’ authority to determine the term of barangay officials does not include the power to prolong the existing term of incumbents after they have been elected.

Macalintal also rejected the government’s characterization of the 2028 election date as merely an “incidental setting,” arguing that moving an election to a later date constitutes a postponement when it keeps incumbents in office beyond the period for which they were elected.

Macalintal also disputed the government’s reliance on governance continuity and multiyear projects, saying these reasons did not satisfy the standards previously laid down by the SC for postponing elections.
He challenged the administration’s reasons for retaining incumbent barangay officials, including their role in crime prevention, flood response and garbage collection. — Christine Boton

articles.title: ICC prosecutor opposes evidence disclosure cap in Duterte’s case
articles.summary: The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court has opposed the request of former president Rodrigo Duterte’s lawyers to limit the documents disclosed in relation to his upcoming crimes…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has opposed the request of former president Rodrigo Duterte’s lawyers to limit the documents disclosed in relation to his upcoming crimes against humanity trial.
In his 16-page response released yesterday, ICC acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang maintained that the documents disclosed to the defense are reasonable and relevant to the case.

He was responding to defense lawyer Peter Haynes’ allegations that the prosecution provided them with a “sheer volume of material” that supposedly undermines Duterte’s right to adequate time for preparation of his defense.

“The prosecution rejects the repeated portrayal of the disclosure of documents that memorialize the attack against the civilian population, including victims specified in this case, as the ‘dumping of documents’ into the case record,” read the prosecution’s response.

“The prosecution’s disclosure is further reasonable, considering the large geographic and temporal scope of this case and the fact that the accused is a former head of state who openly ran a ‘war on drugs’ that drew significant domestic and international attention. The volume of the prosecution’s List of Evidence is also consistent with that of other cases at this Court,” it added.
In his original request, Haynes asked the Trial Chamber III to act on what it described as “voluminous” documents disclosed by the prosecution ahead of the trial.
He noted that from the initial 5,275 items of evidence during the confirmation phase, the prosecution has now expanded it to 62,130 items.

“The defense has no ability to read this volume of evidence prior to trial. However, even a cursory review demonstrates that much of the disclosed material is of extremely limited or no relevance to the charges in this case,” said Haynes.
Niang, however, responded by pointing out that majority of its disclosure came from a dataset containing “highly relevant” information.
He said the prosecution has taken reasonable steps to help the defense review the dataset, including summaries of incidents in the documents.

“Setting an arbitrary cap on the number of documents the prosecution can disclose would automatically place the prosecution in violation of its disclosure obligations as it would require the prosecution to withhold evidence that it considers material to the defense’s preparation,” wrote Niang.

“The prosecution respectfully submits that withholding material evidence from the defense, or forcing the prosecution to remove a dataset that directly supports the contextual elements of its case, would more severely hinder the search for the truth in this case,” he added. — Bella Cariaso

articles.title: P50 million from other countries flowed to Duterte-linked firm
articles.summary: Apart from China, eight other countries – some of which are notorious for money laundering – had been the sources of nearly P50 million in remittances that flowed into a food company…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am

Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo asks Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Atty. Ronel Buenaventura if he is still nervous while testifying during the second day of the impeachment trial on October 6, 2026.
Ryan Baldemor / The Philippine STAR

MANILA, Philippines — Apart from China, eight other countries – some of which are notorious for money laundering – had been the sources of nearly P50 million in remittances that flowed into a food company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio.

Records flashed on screen yesterday on Day 34 of the impeachment trial of Duterte showed that inflows of funds to CALE88 Foods Corp. also came from Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Lithuania, South Africa, Tajikistan, the United Arab Emirates and the United States.
Senator-judges pressed for a breakdown of the foreign funds and questioned the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) if it had ever moved to freeze the accounts.

Based on data flashed by House of Representatives prosecutors, CALE88 received P12.8 million from Russia, P12 million from Ukraine, P7.24 million from Kazakhstan, P6.23 from Lithuania, P6 million from South Africa, P3.8 million from Tajikistan, P684,456 from UAE and nearly P600,000 from the US.

Sen. Raffy Tulfo grilled AMLC executive director Ronel Buenaventura on whether the AMLC had ever unilaterally petitioned the Court of Appeals (CA) for a freeze order on CALE88’s accounts or demanded contracts justifying the purpose of the deposits.

Tulfo also questioned why the council did not flag the non-Chinese inflows despite the reputation of some of the countries as money laundering haven. “Don’t you find it suspicious that a large part of the funds that went to CALE88 came from countries with critical reputation for money laundering like Russia, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, South Africa, di ba kayo nagduda doon?”

Buenaventura declined to make conclusions and apologized to the court. “I have no personal knowledge on the current status of the countries mentioned or their financial or money laundering standing in the international community,” he said.
Requirement
He also said during direct examination by private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia that banks are required by law – not just encouraged – to report all suspicious transactions to AMLC.
“The law used the word ‘required.’ So they’re required to report suspicious transactions. The law did not mention any threshold. The law says regardless of the amount,” Buenaventura said.
“A suspicious transaction could be higher than the threshold or it could be lower than the threshold, as long as the presence of suspicious circumstances are there,” he said.

“Essentially, suspicion is one based on the knowledge of the covered person or reporting entity, based on the profile of the client and taking account all other circumstances to determine whether or not there is a suspicious circumstance,” Buenaventura said.
“The threshold, at least insofar as the law requires, is suspicion or suspicious circumstances,” he added.
But defense counsel Mark Vinluan insisted that such bank records are covered by the confidentiality rule.
“Covered institutions are required to report suspicious transactions. They are not just encouraged to report suspicious transactions,” Divinagracia said in response. — Delon Porcalla, Daphne Galvez

articles.title: DOE: Blackouts, higher power bills loom amid El Niño
articles.summary: Filipinos could face more frequent power outages and higher electricity bills as the country braces for the impact of a “super El Niño,” Energy Secretary Sharon Garin warned…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Filipinos could face more frequent power outages and higher electricity bills as the country braces for the impact of a “super El Niño,” Energy Secretary Sharon Garin warned yesterday.
Prolonged periods of extreme heat could strain coal-fired power plants and deplete water resources needed by hydroelectric facilities, she noted.
“I don’t want to be a doomsayer, but I just want to be very transparent about this,” Garin said on the sidelines of the 44th ASEAN Ministers on Energy Meeting.
The Department of Energy (DOE) is working with the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) to monitor the electricity spot market and prevent potential abuse by industry players.
In August, electricity spot prices in the Visayas and Mindanao surged to nearly P20 per kilowatt-hour before the ERC intervened to mitigate the rates.
These challenges come as the Philippines continues to grapple with an ongoing energy emergency brought by the Middle East conflict.
Amid these concerns, Garin appealed to the public to conserve electricity and practice energy-saving measures.
106 cities, towns in state of calamity
Around 106 cities and towns in five regions are under a state of calamity due to El Niño, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction Management Council.
The NDRRMC said affected localities include 66 in Cagayan Valley, 23 in Caraga, 12 in Bicol and one in Soccsksargen.
Damage to agriculture has reached over P5.4 billion especially in Cagayan Valley, where current losses stand at over P4.9 billion.
In the Davao Region, losses are over P410 million; Bicol, P37.4 million; Caraga, P22 million; Calabarzon, P19.7 million and Soccsksargen, P12.5 million.
Up to 388,375 people nationwide are affected by El Niño.
As of Oct. 2, there were 39 wild, forest or mountain fires in various areas in Caraga.
More than P39 million worth of food and non-food aid have been provided to 24,618 families, the NDRRMC said.
The Philippine National Police has implemented measures to protect PNP personnel from extreme heat.
PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. yesterday reminded police commanders to ensure their personnel have access to drinking water and appropriate protective gear.
Police unit heads must review deployment plans and consider rotational shifts to limit exposure to extreme temperatures, Nartatez said.
The Department of Health is distributing to local government units El Niño toolkits, which contain information on what illnesses to monitor while El Niño persists until next year.
Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said heat stroke, dengue, cholera and typhoid are on an upward trend during El Niño.
Task force
In Muntinlupa, Mayor Ruffy Biazon has revived the city’s El Niño task force to prepare for the impact of the “very strong” climate phenomenon.
“We’re still not sure about its effects, but it’s important that we are prepared,” Biazon said yesterday.

The task force will monitor areas susceptible to possible water shortages, extreme heat, fire and power interruptions. — Michael Punongbayan, Emmanuel Tupas, Rhodina Villanueva, EJ Macababbad, Allen de Guzman

articles.title: NSC to probe alleged Chinese funding of Duterte-linked firms
articles.summary: The National Security Council will investigate alleged financial inflows from China to Philippine-based companies linked to the family of Vice President Sara Duterte, amid concerns over possible…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte conducts a press conference in Mandaluyong on February 18, 2026.
STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The National Security Council (NSC) will investigate alleged financial inflows from China to Philippine-based companies linked to the family of Vice President Sara Duterte, amid concerns over possible foreign interference and national security implications.

National Security Adviser Eduardo Oban Jr. said the NSC is taking information presented during Duterte’s ongoing Senate impeachment trial seriously and will coordinate with intelligence and investigative agencies to assess the reported transactions.

“While the proceedings remain ongoing and the information presented should be properly examined within established legal processes, the reported transactions and any credible information involving significant foreign financial flows that may bear upon the country’s national security warrants careful, in-depth and responsible assessment,” Oban said.

“The NSC will look into the information presented and, as a matter of policy, continue to task the intelligence and investigative agencies and coordinate with relevant government institutions to assess the national security implications, if any, arising from the reported transactions,” he added.
Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. earlier expressed similar concern over information on alleged Chinese financial links raised by former senator Antonio Trillanes IV.

“The allegations of former senator Trillanes, if substantiated, raise serious implications for national security,” Teodoro said. “He should submit the evidence in his possession, if any, to our law enforcement authorities so the matter can be thoroughly investigated.”
Armed Forces of the Philippines spokesman for the West Philippine Sea, retired rear admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, also pointed to the potential security implications of foreign funding.

“I’d also like to highlight the statement of the National Security Council, of the NSA that the appropriate government agencies are looking into this. And if proven, again, there will be security implications for actions like this,” Trinidad said.

articles.title: Marcos headed to Singapore for meetings, Formula One
articles.summary: President Marcos will undertake a five-day working visit to Singapore that will include watching the Formula One Grand Prix.

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at Malacañang on February 23, 2026.
PPA pool photos by Niño Jesus Orbeta
MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos will undertake a five-day working visit to Singapore that will include watching the Formula One Grand Prix.

Malacañang said the visit aims to discuss ways to expand bilateral ties, promote the Philippines to investors and align the priorities of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to make it more responsive to emerging realities.

The trip to Singapore from Oct. 7 to 11, to be made upon the invitation of Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, will be Marcos’ fifth visit to the Southeast Asian country and his 47th overseas travel since becoming president in 2022.

“The President’s working visit to Singapore underscores the strong relations between the Philippines and Singapore,” Foreign Affairs Assistant Secretary Analyn Ratonel said in a statement issued yesterday.

Ratonel noted the two Southeast Asian countries cooperate across a wide range of areas, including trade, investment, defense and people-to-people ties. The cooperation is also expanding into emerging fields like digital technology, green economy, smart infrastructure, AI, renewable energy and health care, she added.

According to Ratonel, the working visit is timely as it will come ahead of the turnover of the ASEAN chairmanship to Singapore, which she described as a “valued partner” in keeping the regional bloc cohesive and responsive to regional developments.
“It provides an opportunity to further deepen coordination with Singapore and align priorities as the country prepares to assume the ASEAN chairmanship,” the foreign affairs official said.

“We work with (Singapore) on economic integration, maritime cooperation and responses to transnational threats. We also value its consistent support for ASEAN centrality, international law and peaceful dialogue,” Ratonel added.

Marcos will attend the 24th Forbes Global CEO Conference to interact with global business and thought leaders. During the event, Marcos will participate in the “In Conversation” session and will have a one-by-one dialogue with Forbes Media chairman and editor-in-chief Steve Forbes.
“This will be an opportunity for him to showcase the investment and economic priorities in the Philippines’ key growth sectors,” Ratonel said.

Marcos will visit the Singapore Nuclear Research and Safety Institute to learn about the Southeast Asian country’s expertise in nuclear technology and safety and will attend a dinner hosted by Wong on the sidelines of the Formula One Singapore Grand Prix 2026.

“The President has been personally invited by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong to the Singapore Formula 1 Grand Prix. The Singapore Grand Prix brings together government leaders, business executives and investors from around the world,” Ratonel said. “It would provide an opportunity for informal engagements to complement his meetings focused on attracting investment and strengthening the Philippines’ partnerships.”
The officials who will accompany Marcos in the trip include Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Trade Secretary Ma. Cristina Roque and Presidential Communications Secretary Dave Gomez.

Singapore is one of the Philippines’ top trading partners and investors. Two-way trade with Singapore amounted to $9.27 billion last year. Singapore also hosts around 220,000 Filipinos, the 10th largest globally. The Southeast Asian country is also the second largest source of overseas Filipino workers’ remittances, after the US, with $2.098 billion in 2025.

articles.title: Jinggoy on stripping office: It’s standard practice
articles.summary: Detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada yesterday denied there was anything wrong with stripping bare the office of the Senate president pro tempore, calling it “standard practice.”

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian inspects yesterday the former office of Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, which has been stripped bare.
News5
MANILA, Philippines — Detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada yesterday denied there was anything wrong with stripping bare the office of the Senate president pro tempore, calling it “standard practice.”

Estrada issued a statement yesterday in response to news reports that he ordered the office he would vacate and turn over to his successor Sen. Vicente Sotto III stripped bare of all fixtures, tiles and even the toilet, making it look like a construction site.
Estrada claimed his office had notified Sotto’s office that “the fixtures, furnishings and materials in the office would be brought along to the senator’s new office.”

He said the items removed from the office – like floor tiles, glass panels, lighting fixtures and cabinets – “were acquired using personal funds, as the budget provided by the Senate was insufficient to cover all the expenses incurred.”
Estrada said no public funds were used in removing all the fixtures from the office.

“It bears noting that standard practice in the Senate is for the senator occupying an office to renovate the space based on the budget provided, with any expense beyond that shouldered entirely by the occupant. Let it be stressed, in no uncertain terms, that not a single centavo of public funds was wasted,” Estrada said.

“In fact, the Senate will bear no cost whatsoever for office supplies and materials, as most, if not all, of those used in the previous office will simply be re-used in the new one. If anything, this practice reflects prudence and efficiency, not controversy,” he added.
Estrada asked that the “routine administrative transition… not be unnecessarily politicized, sensationalized or made into a manufactured controversy where none exists.”
Sen. Panfilo Lacson came to the defense of Sotto, as he belied Estrada’s claim it was standard practice to turn over a bare office to the successor.
“Poor Senate President Pro Tempore Tito Sotto. Using a monobloc table and chair and gas lamp,” Lacson said, tweeting an AI-generated photo of Sotto writing on a plastic table beside a lampshade.

“I take exception to the statement pertaining to the state or condition of the same Pro Tempore office that I turned over to Sen. Estrada in 2022. Nothing was removed nor destroyed, precisely because government funds were used when I refurbished it when it was turned over to me,” Lacson said.

articles.title: MMDA takes action vs NCAP text scams
articles.summary: Text messages posing as alerts about the no-contact apprehension policy have been flagged by the Metro Manila Development Authority.

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am
MMDA Chairman Romando Artes has filed a complaint regarding the text scams.
Philstar.com / EC Toledo
MANILA, Philippines — Text messages posing as alerts about the no-contact apprehension policy (NCAP) have been flagged by the Metro Manila Development Authority.

At a press briefing, Artes said he wrote to the Department of Information and Communications Technology along with the Credit Information Corp., noting that the MMDA has no power to apprehend scammers.
“We do not have the capability to catch them. We have to rely on law enforcement agencies to capture scammers,” he said.
The police Anti-Cybercrime Group is investigating the fraudulent scheme.
Artes said people should coordinate with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas or Anti-Money Laundering Council to halt the payment system.
“We will coordinate on how to stop the entry and exit of payment to scammers,” he said.
Artes warned motorists about text scams using credit cards as they are more rampant in using NCAP to access information.
Despite the irregularities, Artes encouraged the use of NCAP, saying it eases traffic congestion.
Artes said he is coordinating with local government units to address concerns regarding NCAP.
In June, three Supreme Court justices said issues linked to NCAP must be resolved, such as the honorarium provision in the joint venture agreement with QPax Traffic Systems Inc.
Manila Mayor Isko Moreno yesterday said they will pursue the implementation of NCAP.

“We want to resolve the abuses of traffic enforcers for the longest time. We will be disciplined by this policy. Kotong will be removed,” Moreno said, referring to law enforcers demanding bribes. — Ghio Ong, Emmanuel Tupas, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: Bank records show undeclared VP assets
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has begun looking into the bank records of Vice President Sara Duterte, uncovering 30 active accounts containing P190 million or way above the P13.32 million declared in…

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court has begun looking into the bank records of Vice President Sara Duterte, uncovering 30 active accounts containing P190 million or way above the P13.32 million declared in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN).
The financial records were gathered from eight banks between 2022 and 2025. The information on her bank records emerged yesterday on Day 34 of her impeachment trial.

During the proceedings, details of her and her husband Manases Carpio’s bank accounts were made public as House prosecutors move to pin her down for alleged unexplained wealth under Article II of the Articles of Impeachment.
The Duterte spouses’ accounts held more than P59 million in 2022, more than P71 million the following year, more than P22 million in 2024 and more than P35 million in 2025.

The more than P190 million presented by the prosecution was a combination of four separate year-end snapshots. It is not an account balance held on a single date. The prosecution intends to compare each year’s balance with the SALN covering the same year.
Rep. Joel Chua, one of the prosecutors, revealed all these accounts couldn’t be found in the Vice President’s SALNs.

He said Carpio listed P8 million under “other personal properties,” described as “various,” in the 2022 SALN. Duterte listed two amounts under the same category: P2.25 million and P3 million. Her entries totaled P5.25 million.

Combined, their declared “other personal properties” amounted to P13.325 million. Against the prosecution’s delivered figure of more than P59 million in year-end bank balances, the difference exceeds P45.675 million.
“In this tabulation alone, it really doesn’t add up, the gap is big,” Chua said.
The comparison does not add balances from different years. It places the balance recorded at the end of 2022 beside the SALN for the same year.
Chua said the couple’s declared net worth for 2022 was approximately P71 million. The offered bank balance alone would account for most of that amount before other declared assets were counted.
He also referred to firearms worth approximately P7 million presented in earlier testimony as among the assets that would have to fit within the same declared net worth.
Money laundering

The impeachment court also tackled yesterday the possibility that CALE88 Foods Corp., a food manufacturing company linked to Carpio, may have been used for money laundering after it allegedly received funds from China. Carpio holds a 47.5 percent share in CALE88, which received P319 million “remittance” from Chinese companies, the prosecution earlier said.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian quizzed Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) executive director Ronel Buenaventura about red flags based on the firm’s balance sheet.

Gatchalian said CALE88 had P776 million “inflow” and P154 million “outflow,” even though cumulative sales only amounted to P23 million, assets at P18 million, liabilities at P20 million and a paid-up capital of only P125,000.
He noted that half of CALE88 sales “came from China,” as he pressed AMLC to also look into the legitimacy of the Chinese entities pouring in the funds.

When Buenaventura said he could not testify beyond what was asked of him in the court subpoena, Gatchalian pressed his point that the banks flagged transactions linked to Cale88 because of “no underlying legal or trade obligation purpose or economic justification.”
Buenaventura said he does not want to add to the interpretation of why it was flagged suspicious.
Gatchalian asked Buenaventura if CALE88 could be considered a “candidate for money laundering” because its books did not show where the P776-million inflow came from.
Buenaventura said CALE88 can be considered a candidate for money laundering, subject to further investigation.
“In general po, we have to determine if there is unlawful activity or transaction that generated the funds,” Buenaventura said.
In his interjection, Sen. Francis Pangilinan said CALE88 received the funds from China during the period 2022 to 2025, or when Duterte is already the vice president. Buenaventura agreed.
He added that total aggregated amount that went to Cale88 according to covered and suspicious transaction reports amounted to P1,254,736,297.08.
Asked by Sen. Erwin Tulfo if the receipt of funds from China was tantamount to a “conflict of interest,” Buenaventura begged off from giving an opinion.
When Tulfo asked if there is “factual basis” to determine if the source of the funds was “legal or illegal,” Buenaventura said he is leaving it up to the court to make a conclusion.
China links
Also during the proceedings, some senator-judges expressed intention to dig deeper to uncover potential links between Beijing state-owned businesses and some local political groups.
Sen. Risa Hontiveros confronted Buenaventura over the P319 million in remittances from China to Cale88.

Hontiveros said her office conducted its own corporate background checks on several remitters and found them to be tied directly to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Beijing’s foreign policy arms.

She said one of the senders of the money to CALE88, Beijing Zhenweifang Food Co., is owned by Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group, an enterprise with an embedded CCP apparatus including its own Party Committee and 11 subordinate party branches.

She added that Beijing Zhenweifang’s chairman belongs to the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), a body cited in international intelligence reports as the “premier overt United Front organization” for foreign interference.

“Why is this important, Attorney Buenaventura? Because this Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group is not an ordinary company. It’s a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party,” Hontiveros stressed.
Buenaventura declined to characterize the transactions as a cause for concern, saying he needs to review the background of the entities.

The push to investigate Chinese funding extended to political organizations supporting the Duterte family, with Sen. Bam Aquino citing the Chinese government’s denial of donations to the Tapang at Malasakit alliance.

After Buenaventura confirmed that records of Tapang at Malasakit were not included in the AMLC subpoena, presiding office Francis Escudero observed that the group might not fall under the agency’s regulatory scope.
“If I may, Tapang at Malasakit is not a juridical entity I believe… that may have an account or a policy covered by the AMLC,” Escudero said. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Neil Jayson Servallos

articles.title: Works by Canadian authors Margaret Atwood and Ryan North among books banned in U.S. schools
articles.summary: Nearly 12,000 bans took place in American public schools over the past year, according to a new study from PEN America, the highest total since the free expression organization began tracking…

image.caption: The Handmaid's Tale is a book by Margaret Atwood. (Angela Weiss/AFP via Getty Images)

blocks.text: Books

Nearly 12,000 bans took place in American public schools over the past year, according to a new study from PEN America, the highest total since the free expression organization began tracking removals five years ago.
A record high for book bans in American schools in 2026, according to PEN America
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Oct 06, 2026 11:59 AM EDT | Last Updated: 13 minutes ago
Nearly 12,000 bans took place in American public schools over the past year, according to a new study from PEN America.
This is the highest total since the free expression organization began tracking removals five years ago.

The report arrives during the international Banned Books Week, which runs from Oct. 4 to Oct. 10. This year’s theme is "Let Books Be. Protect the Freedom to Read", during which events at U.S.-based schools and libraries and other locations call attention to censorship efforts.
While Canada marks its dedicated intellectual freedom campaign in February, some Canadian libraries and bookstores engage in global outreach and displays during this October window.

For the second straight year, American author Stephen King was the author most likely to have his work withdrawn. King’s books were pulled 312 times, with The Shining and The Green Mile among those impacted.

Also among the banned novels in American schools is Canadian author Margaret Atwood’s The Handmaid’s Tale, the classic dystopian novel about a totalitarian society in what used to be part of the United States.

items: The Handmaid's Tale turns 40, and special events are being held around the world to pay tribute

blocks.text: The most banned individual title was Patrick McCormick’s novel about a girl sold into sexual slavery in India, Sold, for which PEN found 25 removals.
Other books commonly targeted include Laurie Halse Anderson’s Speak, her prize-winning novel about a teenager who falls silent after being raped; Ellen Hopkins’ novel about drug addiction, Crank.
(Riverhead Books)

Several titles appear in PEN America’s Index of School Book Bans for the first time during the 2025-2026 school year, including classic novels, gamebook adaptations, popular fiction and coming-of-age young adult stories, manga, and an anthology on feminism.
Among these titles is Romeo and/or Juliet: A Chooseable Path Adventure, a 2016 graphic novel by Ottawa-born webcomic and comic book writer Ryan North.

Many of the bans took place in Florida and Texas, where restrictive laws have been passed and both politicians and conservative activists have pushed for removals. PEN has also found that school district administrators rely increasingly on AI to determine which books should be pulled.

items: 12 Canadian comics we're excited to read this fall

blocks.text: Themes of race, racism, sexuality and gender identity remain the most common reasons books are challenged.

“School libraries make knowledge and ideas available, ensure books remain available for all regardless of personal or political ideologies, and open gateways to stories that inform, challenge, and reflect the realities of the world back to readers,” the PEN report, titled Banned in the USA, reads in part.
“Book bans impede the freedom to read, cutting students’ access to a diversity of views, voices, perspectives, and literature they deserve to encounter.”

In all, PEN found 11,982 cases of bans, affecting 7,370 individual works. Over 4,500 were on the list for the first time, ranging from the 19th century classic Jane Eyre to Sui Ishida’s Tokyo Ghoul manga series.

PEN America and the American Library Association have both reported historic surges in bans since the early 2020s, although their methodologies differ. PEN counts books removed even for a short time as a ban, while the ALA only includes books that have been permanently pulled.
According to the library association’s most recent report, published in April, some 5,600 instances of bans took place during the previous year.
- with files from CBC Books

articles.title: Direct spending on Canadian military could reach more than $163B by 2035: budget watchdog
articles.summary: Direct spending on the Canadian military could reach $163.6 billion by 2035 under the Liberal government's proposal to meet NATO's benchmark target of five per cent of GDP, the Parliamentary Budget…

image.caption: A scale model of a ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems HDW Class 212CD submarine is shown at the Canadian Association of Defence and Security Industries annual trade show, CANSEC, in Ottawa on May 27. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

Direct spending on the Canadian military could reach $163.6 billion by 2035 under the Liberal government's proposal to meet NATO's benchmark target of five per cent of GDP, the Parliamentary Budget Office in a new report on Tuesday.
Parliamentary Budget Office report says many unknowns remain, which could affect government finances

Direct spending on the Canadian military could reach $163.6 billion by 2035 under the Liberal government's proposal to meet NATO's benchmark target of five per cent of GDP, the Parliamentary Budget Office said Tuesday.
However, a lot of unknowns remain that could affect government finances down the road, the fiscal watchdog said in a new report.

"Meeting Canada's defence commitments will require substantial increases in government expenditure and investment, with important implications for economic activity, industrial capacity and the composition of production in Canada," said the report penned by PBO researchers.

Since the federal government uses an accrual method when counting defence expenditures — basically recording money when it is earned, and paying bills when they are owed, not when cash actually changes hands — the impact "would increase the budgetary deficit by $63.7 billion, or 1.4 per cent of GDP," the PBO said.

What the fiscal pain might be will depend on how Prime Minister Mark Carney's government manages the increase. The PBO presents two scenarios: one where there's a gradual, steady increase in the buying of new equipment and the other where purchases are postponed.

items: Canada's next defence fight won’t be over spending. It’ll be over trust
Ottawa plans Crown corporation to break defence procurement logjam

blocks.text: Under both the Liberal government of Justin Trudeau and the Conservative government of Stephen Harper, it became routine to postpone big-ticket equipment purchases. Money from some of those items was reprofiled to later years; in other cases, the funds lapsed and were returned to the federal treasury.
In a previous report, the PBO tracked more than $18 billion set aside for military spending that lapsed under the Trudeau government.

Carney ordered the injection of $9 billion into defence last year in order for Canada to meet the old NATO spending benchmark of two per cent of gross domestic product. The new target of five per cent of GDP — 3.5 per cent on direct military spending and 1.5 per cent on defence infrastructure — is to be phased in gradually over the next decade.
Carney has said the plan is for Canada to hit a four per cent target on defence spending — 2.5 per cent and 1.5 per cent — by 2030.
Parliamentary Budget Officer Annette Ryan appears at the Commons committee on government operations and estimates on Parliament Hill in Ottawa on June 16. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

Annette Ryan, who took over as parliamentary budget officer in the spring, told the House of Commons defence committee on Monday that the government's plan to reach the new target after 2030 is still a work in progress.
"It'll take some time before we can actually see the effect of all of these investments," she told committee MPs.
Ryan said the PBO has begun work to model what sort of economic impact the drastic increase in defence spending will have on federal finances and the Canadian economy.
"This is a very rapid increase," Ryan said in French, noting there are procurement risks.

"I think that Canada's industrial capacity may not be able to meet the need, which is a risk.… And we might ask, what are we getting back from all of these industrial and technological purchases? That's another source of risk," she said. "So yes, there are a number of risks associated with these very significant sums of money."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Murray Brewster is the senior defence writer for CBC News, based in Ottawa. He has covered the Canadian military and foreign policy from Parliament Hill for over a decade. Among other assignments, he spent a total of 15 months on the ground covering the Afghan war for The Canadian Press. Prior to that, he covered defence issues and politics for CP in Nova Scotia for 11 years and was bureau chief for Standard Broadcast News in Ottawa.

articles.title: ‘This is state violence’: Paris students rage at politicians and heavy-handed policing
articles.summary: Unprecedented protests that began in low-income banlieue are turning ugly, with investigations under way into police brutality

blocks.text: Before dawn on Tuesday outside the Lycée Sophie-Germain in central Paris, hundreds of teenagers dragged wheelie bins, metal barriers and shopping trolleys to build a barricade outside the front door of their secondary school.

Climbing to the top of the piles of bins, pupils held banners calling for more funding and greater equality in French schools. But they were also protesting against French riot police, who have been accused by human rights groups of using disproportionate force against children in what is fast becoming the biggest youth protest movement in decades.

“Everyone hates the police,” chanted a group of 15- and 16-year-olds. At least 215 teenagers, 715 police officers and 85 teaching staff have been injured in clashes in recent days, according to the government.

“We’re teenagers with wheelie bins, and the police have heavy weapons, it’s totally mismatched,” said Livia, 17, who was studying theatre at a lycée in northern Paris and did not want her real name published. “The police are extremely violent in France. This is state violence and it’s horrible seeing police allowed to target children. It’s important to remember this is institutionalised violence, it’s planned and deliberate.”

blocks.caption: A large student protest in Nantes on Tuesday. Photograph: Stéphane Mahé/Reuters

blocks.text: Ten investigations into possible police brutality are under way after injuries allegedly involving the use of police weapons, including one 15-year-old who lost his hand, another who lost his eye and a boy whose jaw and teeth were shattered, leaving him, as his mother said, barely able to eat with a straw in hospital.

“The policing is catastrophic, people have been mutilated by weapons – one boy has lost an eye – it’s horrible,” said Lily, 17 (not her real name), who was studying social sciences in her final year of school and demonstrating for more funding in what she called a discriminatory education system that left poorer children behind. “My parents support me being on the barricades and at the protests. They’re worried about the policing, but they said they’d come and get me from the police station if I was arrested.”

blocks.caption: French riot police in Lyon on Tuesday. Photograph: Denis Balibouse/Reuters

blocks.text: Teenagers nearby held up cardboard signs protesting against the use of teargas and riot police. “A state that gases high school students is a weak state,” read one banner. “Gas rapists, not children,” said another sign in reference to calls for tougher laws against sexual violence. Another banner read: “Not here to riot.”
The unprecedented protest movement that began outside one school in a low-income Paris suburb has spread across the country, taking the government by surprise.

blocks.caption: Students take part in protests across France

blocks.text: Hundreds of high schools have been barricaded and forced to close as pupils protest against teacher shortages, crumbling buildings and overcrowded classes. The justice ministry said 5,060 people had been arrested ⁠since the protests began, 87% of them being minors. More than 1,800 people had been prosecuted, ​including 1,483 minors, the ministry said, without specifying ​the crimes. It said 790 cases had been ​dismissed. The government said 24 schools had been burned or ransacked.

“In more than 20 years of teaching, I’ve never seen protests this big,” said one teacher at Sophie-Germain high school who planned to join the Paris demonstration on Tuesday afternoon. “The students in central Paris have shown a great sense of solidarity with those in the Paris suburbs who face much worse conditions in their schools. There’s a feeling of solidarity and generosity between teenagers that flies in the face of the notion that we live in an era of selfishness. No one knows how long this will go on for.”

blocks.caption: A protester in Montpellier on Friday. Photograph: Horcajuelo Guillaume/EPA

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of students, trade unionists and parents are expected to march in support of the protests across France on Tuesday afternoon, including in Paris, Toulouse, Nice and Bordeaux, with riot police on alert.

Isabella, 16, said she had the backing of her parents, who work in film and music. “Young people have been teargassed for doing nothing but trying to express their opinion. Everybody told us that school was the great leveller, but today that is not the case at all. A teenager in the banlieue [suburbs] of Paris is never going to have the same opportunities as a student from the city centre. That’s why we’re here today.”
after newsletter promotion
Lionel, 17, who was in his final year at school and hoped to study English, said: “The aim isn’t to riot or smash things up, we just want to protest peacefully.”

blocks.caption: Demonstrations in Paris on Tuesday. Photograph: Tom Nicholson/Reuters

blocks.text: Teenagers also chanted songs against Marine Le Pen, the far-right, anti-immigration candidate in the 2027 presidential election, who is high in the polls as Emmanuel Macron steps down after a decade in office. Many teenagers were worried about the election. “We’re also protesting against the growth of the far right,” said Aislinn.

Justine, 17, who had been at the barricade since before dawn, said she hoped the protest would continue and grow into a “massive” movement. “For years, there has been a mental health crisis among young people in France and anger at rundown schools and the stresses of the education system. We need the government to listen to us and make radical change.”

Maya, an 18-year-old sports science student, had spent two days on a barricade at her university building in Bobigny in solidarity with school students, and joined the Paris protest march on Tuesday. She had attended high school in Drancy in Seine-Saint-Denis outside Paris, in a school she said had mould on the walls, not enough chairs for class and absent teachers who often were not replaced.

“It’s only when we spoke to other students at university who came from different types of schools in the countryside or city centres that we realised our experience was so different and that there was a real injustice to the conditions we had to learn in,” she said.

blocks.caption: Protests in Lyon on Tuesday. Photograph: Denis Balibouse/Reuters

blocks.text: Julie, 46, a self-employed parent of two high school children from Levallois, in the west of Paris, had joined her husband to accompany her sons to the Paris march. She said: “We’re here to support our children but also to protect them from what is going on with the police and the violence we’ve seen with the police these last few days. We’ve seen our own child teargassed many times in front of his school ... It’s unbelievable.”
Students’ names have been changed.

articles.title: State parliament elects Germany’s first far-right speaker since second world war
articles.summary: Tobias Rausch secures role of president in Saxony-Anhalt after AfD’s election breakthrough

blocks.text: Alternative für Deutschland has become Germany’s first far-right party to secure the position of speaker of a regional parliament since the second world war.
Tobias Rausch, a former estate agent, was elected in the first round of voting on Tuesday in Saxony-Anhalt. He won 48 out of the 82 votes cast.
Later in the day, Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, part of the AfD’s more extreme wing, was elected as Rausch’s deputy.

The AfD, which is classed as “rightwing extremist” by the eastern state’s intelligence agency, won nearly 44% of votes in elections last month, dealing a hammer blow to Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, and his centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU).

Rausch’s election to the role of president of the parliament – and its speaker – took place at the inaugural gathering of members in the state capital, Magdeburg. Twenty-nine voted against Rausch and five abstained.

blocks.caption: Protesters console each other outside the state parliament in Magdeburg after the election of Tobias Rausch as speaker on Tuesday. Photograph: Maja Hitij/Getty Images

blocks.text: The AfD parliamentary group holds 39 seats, narrowly short of an absolute majority. Five politicians from the BSW, a small leftwing party that echoes the AfD’s stances on Russia and immigration, had already said they would vote for Rausch. Tuesday’s result means that four other MPs voted for the 35-year-old in the secret ballot.

The willingness of politicians to break the “firewall” – a moral agreement among other parties to shun the AfD – gives the party a chance of being able to form a government in the state – a feat it had looked unlikely to pull off. This would be even more of a historical watershed in postwar Germany.

The BSW’s support for Rausch came after the party’s founder, Sahra Wagenknecht, declared it was time to do away with “firewall idiocy”. Her deputy, Christian Leye, said the “firewall is not working” and the votes of nearly 44% of electors could not be ignored.
“We need an intelligent way of dealing with the AfD and that means dealing with the content of their programme instead of a firewall,” Leye told German media.

blocks.caption: Hans-Thomas Tillschneider in the state parliament after being elected deputy speaker on Tuesday. He is being lined up as Saxony-Anhalt’s culture and science minister. Photograph: Ronny Hartmann/Reuters

blocks.text: It was not immediately clear who was behind Tillschneider’s election because the BSW had said it would refuse to vote for him. He received 44 votes.

As the architect of the AfD’s “radical” manifesto, he is lined up to become culture and science minister in the state. He has referred to the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, as “a real man with a sound set of values” and accused immigrants of “streaming in here in masses … wanting to squander our money”.
Tillschneider is a scholar of Islamic studies who has described Islam as a “fungus” growing on the “German oak”. His family emigrated from Romania to Germany in the 1980s.

In his acceptance speech, Rausch promised to represent all voices and “take different opinions seriously and to try to take decisions in a transparent way”. He was applauded by his own parliamentary group and the ranks of the BSW. The other MPs did not respond.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Demonstrators read the German constitution during a protest outside Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament on Tuesday. Photograph: Ronny Hartmann/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Rausch was one of the key figures in a nepotism scandal over AfD MPs employing family members in parliament. He denied claims that several of his siblings and a brother-in-law were working in the state parliament but confirmed he was employing several players from the football club where he is a member.

He is a close ally and confidant of Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD’s lead candidate, who is positioning himself to take over as leader of Saxony-Anhalt. He has yet to say which parties or politicians have agreed to cooperate with the AfD, only that “negotiations are going well”. The AfD claims to be courting members of the CDU to break the firewall, a claim CDU leaders deny.
The BSW says it will support an AfD-led parliament only if a nonpartisan figure is appointed to lead it, a position the AfD rejects. Siegmund has until December to form a government.

Opposition MPs raised alarm over the breaching of the firewall. “Whoever has invested a representative of extremist and anti-constitutional party with this office will bear responsibility for the consequences,” said Green MP Susan Sziborra-Seidlitz, to loud applause.

The result of the Saxony-Anhalt poll, along with two other regional elections in September, has piled huge pressure on Merz, who pledged on taking office in 2025 that he would halve the AfD’s support by boosting the economy and reducing immigration. Instead, the CDU’s support has more or less halved and that of the AfD has surged to 30% in national polls.

Before the vote, Eva von Angern of the leftwing Die Linke party and the longest-serving member of the Saxony-Anhalt parliament, drew parallels between Rausch’s election to the post of speaker, and Hermann Göring’s use of that role in the Reichstag in the 1930s to facilitate Adolf Hitler’s rise to power.
She claimed that the negative consequences of the AfD’s win in the state were already being felt in lower tourist numbers and teachers withdrawing job applications.

articles.title: UK: Seventh arrest made after air base plot
articles.summary: The man, a British national in his twenties, was arrested in London in suspicion of "preparing terrorist acts."

image.caption: The US military's B1 bombers were withdrawn from RAF FairfordImage: Alastair Grant/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Police in the UK arrested a man in connection with an alleged planned attack on a military air base used by the United States.
The suspect, a 22-year-old British national, was arrested "on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts," police said.

Police arrested the man in London, and he is the seventh person taken into custody in connection with the incident in which three vans were stopped near the RAF Fairford air base in England's southwest on September 27.
While no explosives were found in the van, police secured some gasoline in them, it said.
The other six suspects were also men in their 20s, including one who is a dual UK-Iranian national. All six have been released on bail.
Media reports in the UK said one of the initial suspects had informed the authorities of the incident, which police did not confirm.

blocks.caption: Police were alerted to suspicious activity next to the RAF Fairford baseImage: Alastair Grant/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Bombers withdrawn
US bombers have been seen taking off and landing at the air base, with the UK government allowing Washington to use it for "specific defensive operations into Iran."

US President Donald Trump said Washington had withdrawn all B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford due to "threats" possibly linked to Iran. At the same time, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio played down specific threats.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham also said there were "strong indications" that Iranhad a role in the incident, with British authorities labeling it "major." The UK also insists the RAF Fairford air base is safe.
Tehran rejected any involvement.

articles.title: Defense: No proof Sara Duterte, husband's millions came from Chinese gov't
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte"s defense team maintained that there is no proof directly linking millions of pesos in her and her husband"s bank accounts to funds from the Chinese government.

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team maintained that there is no proof directly linking millions of pesos in her and her husband’s bank accounts to funds from the Chinese government.

In a “24 Oras” report by Joseph Morong on Tuesday, transaction records from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) showed that an estimated P4.4 billion went in and out of the accounts of the Vice President and her husband, Atty. Mans Carpio, from 2007 to 2025.

Meanwhile, over P5.3 billion in covered and suspicious transactions were flagged across 15 companies linked to the couple. Among these is Cale88 Foods Corporation, which reportedly received an estimated P319 million from China and Hong Kong.
The Vice President also declared Cale88 in her 2025 Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).
“Records of AMLC show that China, as a country, funneled funds to Cale88, correct?” Defense lawyer Mark Vinluan asked AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura, who was called as a witness.
“As far as I recall and based on record, there is no showing here,” Buenaventura answered.
The defense team also asserted that having recorded transactions does not automatically mean the money went directly to the Vice President and her husband.
“Does the AMLC have any record of how much of these transactions by Cale88 Foods Corporation redounded to the benefit of VP Sara and Attorney Mans?” Vinluan asked the witness.
“Redounded the benefit, Your Honor. There is none. There's none,” Buenaventura answered.
State-owned companies
During interjections by some senator-judges, they flagged several companies recorded in the transactions as state-owned Chinese entities.
“Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group, it's a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party,” Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros pointed out.

“Sa mismong corporate governance structure, Xinjiang Fruit, by institutional Chinese Communist Party organization na naka-embed. It has its own Chinese Communist Party committee, party committee organization department, and 11 subordinate subcommittees or party branches,” she added.

(In its very corporate governance structure, Xinjiang Fruit has an embedded Chinese Communist Party organization. It has its own Chinese Communist Party committee, party committee organization department, and 11 subordinate subcommittees or party branches.)

Meanwhile, Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo circled back to Cale88, asking whether it was suspicious that millions of pesos entering the company originated from countries with a critical reputation for money laundering.

“Hindi ba kaduda-duda na karamihan sa milyones na pondo na pumasok sa Cale88 ay galing sa mga bansang may kritikal na reputasyon sa money laundering gaya ng Russia, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan [at] South Africa?” Tulfo asked the witness.

(Is it not suspicious that most of the millions in funds that entered Cale88 came from countries with a critical reputation in money laundering, such as Russia, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and South Africa?)
“Your Honor… I cannot make a conclusion,” Buenaventura responded.
Mismatch
Duterte’s defense team maintained that a suspicious transaction report (STR) is not a sufficient basis to conclude that the Vice President engaged in illegal transactions.
Vinluan confirmed with Buenaventura whether the filing of an STR is merely a compliance measure rather than a legal determination of unlawful activity.
The witness affirmed this, stating that it is a legal requirement and that no illegality can be concluded solely on the basis of the report.
“It’s therefore not a legal conclusion that there is money laundering, correct? Vinluan asked.
“Yes, Your Honor,” Buenaventura answered.

However, presiding officer Senator Chiz Escudero raised concern that even if Duterte’s declared SALN from 2022 to 2025 and her total salary from 2007 to 2025 were combined, the amount would still fail to match the total value of AMLC transactions.
“It totaled P336M… Hindi pa rin umabot ng P424M. What would explain this huge amount? Posible ba ‘yung in and out?” Escuero asked.
(It totaled P336 million… It still does not reach P424 million. What would explain this huge amount? Is it possible that this represents money moving in and out of the accounts?)
“Hindi ko po masagot, hindi ko po nakita ‘yung SALN. Spread din po as reported to us,” Buenaventura said.
(I cannot answer that; I have not seen the SALN. The amounts were also spread out as reported to us.)
Buenaventura also confirmed, upon questioning by Senator Bam Aquino, that billions of pesos passed through the accounts. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Want to buy GCash shares? How retail investors can join the IPO
articles.summary: Here’s what you need to know about the offer period and what to consider before deciding whether to buy

blocks.text: Here’s what you need to know about the offer period and what to consider before deciding whether to buy

items: Filipinos can invest in GCash through GStocks PH in the GCash app.
Secondary shares sold by existing shareholders make up 80% of GCash's initial public offering.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Filipinos can now buy into GCash before it officially makes its Philippine Stock Exchange debut, with the public offer period starting Tuesday, October 6.

One of the easiest routes is through GStocks PH inside the GCash app itself. Investors can open Invest, select GStocks PH, then tap the IPO banner. GStocks PH requires an eligible account with enough money in its trading wallet. Opening an account generally requires users to be at least 18 years old, have a Philippine SIM, a fully verified GCash account, and a valid government ID.
The minimum GCash IPO order through GStocks PH is 100 shares, worth P660 at the P6.60 offer price.

Retail investors can also participate as local small investors through PSE EASy. The PSE said all LSI subscriptions for the Mynt IPO must be submitted through the platform, which requires investors to nominate a PSE trading participant or broker. The usual LSI ceiling is P100,000. Investors with existing brokerage accounts may also check whether their broker is accepting IPO orders.
The offer period runs until noon on Monday, October 12, giving retail investors until then to submit their subscriptions and complete any required payment and documentation.
Regular trading under the ticker GCASH is scheduled to begin on October 20, when allocated IPO shares can start trading on the PSE.

blocks.caption: For GCash’s early private equity backers, record IPO will be ultimate payday

blocks.text: In an investor briefing on Tuesday, GCash’s top executives made their case for why the homegrown e-wallet is a good buy.

Mynt had 41.5 million monthly active users by June, about four times the active users of its nearest competitor. Its adjusted revenue grew at a 54% compound annual growth rate from 2023 to 2025, while net income rose at a 64.4% CAGR over the same period, reaching P17.25 billion in 2025.

In other words, both revenue and profit were growing quite strongly over that two-year stretch. Net income reached another P10.82 billion in the first half of 2026. Management is eyeing lending, merchant services, overseas users, and deeper use of the app as the next avenue of growth.

But investors also have reasons to look closely at the deal. Around 80% of the IPO consists of secondary shares being sold by existing shareholders, meaning most of the money raised from those shares goes to the sellers rather than Mynt as fresh capital. Management has stressed that this does not represent a full exit by its strategic shareholders, but it does show that several early private equity investors see this as a good time to cash out. (READ: Meet the new cornerstone investors lining up for GCash’s record IPO)

Remember too the oft-repeated investing maxim that a good company can still be a bad investment at the wrong price. GCash is also coming to market at a hefty valuation. At P6.60, its roughly P442-billion valuation works out to about 24.6x its latest trailing 12-month earnings through June, against the PSEi’s 9.87x multiple as of October 2. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge complete: Skydance
articles.summary: Skydance-owned Paramount has closed its $81 billion US takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, further concentrating power in an industry already run by just a handful of major players.

image.caption: Billionaire David Ellison, left, purchased Paramount last year, and will be co-CEO of Skydance, alongside Ynon Kreiz, right, who helped create the Barbie movie as chairman and CEO of Mattel. (Valerie Macon/ AFP, Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images)

blocks.text: It's official: Skydance-owned Paramount has closed its $81 billion US takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery.
The companies completed the deal on Tuesday, ushering in a new Hollywood giant with the now shorter "Skydance" nametag.

The merger brings two of America's oldest moviemaking studios together — and HBO Max, titles ranging from Harry Potter to Sinners and even networks like CNN find themselves under the same roof as Paramount+, CBS and the likes of Top Gun and The Godfather.

All of them will come under the helm of billionaire David Ellison, and his new co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. That further concentrates power in an industry already run by just a handful of major players. Ellison's Skydance bought out Paramount for $8 billion US last year, and set its sights on Warner — an even bigger fish — very soon after.
What followed erupted into a tumultuous, roughly year-long fight over Warner's fate.
Skydance Corp. emerges from one of the biggest tie-ups ever in the media and entertainment industry. Including billions of dollars in debt, the Warner acquisition amounted to nearly $111 billion US.
"Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry," Ellison said in a statement Tuesday.
"We couldn't be more excited to get to work."
Here's a look at some of the key moments that got us here.
Netflix vs. Paramount
The early days of Paramount's quest for Warner turned into a messy bidding war.
Months after disclosing it was open to selling parts or even all of its business, Warner initially struck a studio and streaming deal with Netflix back in December.

But Skydance-owned Paramount, which claimed Warner management "never engaged meaningfully" with its previous proposals, soon launched a hostile counterbid aimed at taking over the entire company — including networks like CNN and Discovery.

The Hollywood giants spent much of early 2026 in a heated back-and-forth over who had a stronger offer on the table, with Warner leadership repeatedly backing Netflix as its preferred suitor. But Paramount eventually upped its offer to buy all of Warner for $31 per share, and Netflix opted to bow out of the race.
Warner and Paramount inked a mutual merger agreement by late February.

Actor Sally Field spoke out against the Paramount-Warner deal when she accepted the award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series during the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards. (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP/ Getty Images)
The response from Hollywood
In April, thousands of movie stars, writers, directors and other professionals announced their "unequivocal opposition" to the Paramount-Warner merger.

The open letter — which was signed by long-outspoken critics of the deal like Jane Fonda and Mark Ruffalo, as well as Hollywood heavyweights from Canadian director Denis Villeneuve to J.J. Abrams — warned of fewer jobs and "less choice for audiences in the United States and around the world."
Meanwhile, some other stars lined up to back Paramount as Ellison reiterated his commitments to the movies.

At CinemaCon this past spring, the company debuted a glossy mini movie about the studio directed by Jon M. Chu and narrated by Tom Cruise — who ended the spot atop the iconic Paramount water tower, with the words "the future is paramount and the future looks pretty great from here." Director James Cameron also doubled down on his support of Ellison.

When accepting her Emmy last month, Remarkably Bright Creatures actor Sally Field — who also signed the open letter in opposition to the Paramount-Warner deal — stressed that "unique storytelling matters" and "we can't let those voices be silenced, or compromised or merged."
Trump and CNN

U.S. President Donald Trump has regularly attacked reporting he deems unfavourable at CNN (most recently attempting to bar the outlet from the White House altogether). Over the course of the Warner buyout, his administration wasn't afraid to chime in about hopes for a new owner.

In December — days after Paramount launched its hostile bid for Warner — Trump said CNN spread "poison and lies," adding that "I think the people who have run CNN for the last long period of time are a disgrace" and "it's imperative that CNN be sold."

The White House took aim again at CNN in March, over the network's coverage of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. At the time, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told reporters that "the sooner David Ellison takes over that network, the better."
Ellison has said editorial independence will be maintained at CNN, the company also agreed to form a "News Editorial Independence Board."

But critics point to turmoil already seen at CBS under Skydance ownership — and aren't convinced this new body will move the needle much, because Ellison is set to have ample oversight over appointments. Outside this board, however, the combined company is retaining Mark Thompson as CNN's editor-in-chief.

David Ellison, right, and wife Sandra Lynn Modic walk to the White House to attend a state dinner hosted for China's President Xi Jinping, last month in Washington. (Carolyn Kaster/The Associated Press)
Trump has held a long relationship with the billionaire Ellison family.
Paramount's chief reportedly hosted a dinner in Washington in Trump's honour back in April, on the same day Warner shareholders gave their greenlight for the merger.

And in June, just two days after the U.S. Justice Department said it wouldn't intervene in the deal, Ellison attended an Ultimate Fighting Championship match on the White House lawn for Trump's 80th birthday (streamed by Paramount+).
Gulf money

To help fund its Warner buyout, Paramount racked up billions of dollars in financial backing from three Gulf countries: Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) approved the company's request for sizeable indirect ownership from those foreign investors.

Paramount previously disclosed it expected those funds to indirectly own nearly 50 per cent of equity interests — but no voting rights — of what is now the larger Skydance. But the company asked for clearance of up to 100 per cent to account for potential future investments, which the FCC granted, citing in part that access to more capital would strengthen the broadcast industry and was therefore "in the public interest."
Critics — including FCC's sole Democratic Commissioner, Anna Gomez — have called the move alarming and unprecedented. They argue that amount of money opens the door to behind-the-scenes influence.

An aerial view of the Paramount logo displayed on the water tower at Paramount Studios in Los Angeles, Calif. A state-led antitrust lawsuit challenging Paramount Skydance's $110 billion US merger with Warner Bros. Discovery was announced as settled in September, clearing a major legal hurdle for the deal. (Mario Tama/Getty Images)
The final antitrust fight
Paramount cleared antitrust hurdles for its Warner acquisition from regulators worldwide over the summer, including the Trump administration's Justice Department.

But in July, Democratic attorneys general from 12 states — led by California's Rob Bonta — sued to block the merger, alleging the combined company would "extinguish competition" and lead to fewer choices for consumers, particularly movie theatergoers and cable customers across the U.S.
The Writers Guild of America followed suit. And Paramount agreed to put its Warner buyout on ice well into next year so the challenges could head toward a larger antitrust trial.

Settlement agreements emerged in September. The states' terms, eventually approved by a judge, include pledges from the company to increase film production in the U.S. over the next five years, commit millions of dollars to a fund aimed at supporting workers displaced by the merger and again establish new editorial monitoring of CNN and CBS.
Settling these challenges marked a key hurdle ahead of closing the deal. Critics decried the deal as capitulating to corporate pressure and said the remedies were too weak.
